verses.text: Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit.
He said, “Amos, what do you see?” I said, “A basket of summer fruit.” Then Yahweh said to me, “The end has come on my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.
The songs of the temple will be wailings in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh. “The dead bodies will be many. In every place they will throw them out with silence.
Hear this, you who desire to swallow up the needy, and cause the poor of the land to fail,

Saying, ‘When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat, making the ephah  small, and the shekel  large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
that we may buy the poor for silver, and the needy for a pair of shoes, and sell the sweepings with the wheat?’”
Yahweh has sworn by the pride of Jacob, “Surely I will never forget any of their works.
Won’t the land tremble for this, and everyone mourn who dwells in it? Yes, it will rise up wholly like the River; and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Egypt.
It will happen in that day,” says the Lord Yahweh, “that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.

I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will make you wear sackcloth on all your bodies, and baldness on every head. I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
Behold, the days come,” says the Lord Yahweh, “that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing Yahweh’s words.
They will wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek Yahweh’s word, and will not find it.
In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint for thirst.
Those who swear by the sin of Samaria, and say, ‘As your god, Dan, lives;’ and, ‘As the way of Beersheba lives;’ they will fall, and never rise up again.”

footnotes.content: A basket of summer fruit—ripe, ready, at the end of the harvest. The Lord uses what Amos sees with his own eyes to make a hard truth plain: the end has come. Sometimes the kindest warning wears the simplest face.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Notice the Lord's own words: I will not again pass by them. He has been patient, turning His face back to them, offering chances to repent. Now He must turn away. When God finally stops pleading, it is because love itself demands the consequences.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The temple songs—once joyful praise—will become wailings. And the dead will be cast out with silence, not honor. This is what happens when a people forget the Lord and build a religion without repentance. The saddest music is the songs that turn to mourning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who desire to swallow up the needy—notice the brutality in that word 'swallow.' The poor are not obstacles to bypass or prices to negotiate; they are human beings whom these merchants are hungry to consume. The Lord sees this hunger, and it grieves Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They count the days until religious observances end so they can return to cheating—making the measure small, the price high, and their balances deceitful. The Sabbath is a burden to them, not a blessing. When worship gets in the way of greed, greed always wins—unless God stops it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They would buy a poor person's freedom for the price of shoes, then mix the rejected grain with the good to sell for full price. Every sin here is deliberate. The Lord does not judge careless wrongs the same way He judges sins done with a calculating heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Yahweh has sworn by His own pride—by His faithfulness and honor—that He will never forget a single act of their injustice. We may think our wrongs are too small to notice, too mixed with good to matter. But God keeps count. His memory is merciful toward the repentant and perfect toward those who remain hardened.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The land will tremble. The River of Egypt rises and sinks—a cycle, a rhythm of judgment and seeming return. But the Lord is using nature itself to speak His word. When the earth trembles, it is because the God who made it is moving in justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sun will go down at noon—darkness at midday. This is not metaphor; it is the terror of a world upside down, of light itself withdrawn. In ancient understanding, the sun was the giver of life and order. Its hiding is the hiding of God's favor, and the people will know it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Feasts become mourning; songs become lamentation. Sackcloth replaces fine garments. The Lord will turn every comfort into sorrow. And the deepest pain: grief like losing an only son—the kind that breaks you entirely. He is showing them that their own treasures cannot save them when judgment comes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A famine of hearing Yahweh's words—not hunger for bread or thirst for water, but the absence of God's voice. This is perhaps the cruelest judgment: the land will be silent. When the Lord stops speaking, no amount of plenty can fill the void. Silence from God is the deepest poverty.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will run from sea to sea, north to east, desperately seeking His word—and will not find it. This is the echo of their own choice: they would not listen when He spoke; now they cannot hear Him when they seek. God's silence is His final answer to those who refuse His voice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the beautiful virgins and young men—those with the most life and strength ahead—will faint for thirst. No one escapes. Judgment is not selective; it falls on all who have built their lives on injustice and refused to turn. Youth and beauty offer no protection.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who swear by idols of Dan and Beersheba—the false gods at the edges of Israel—will fall and never rise again. They built their faith on emptiness; when the judgment comes, there is nothing to hold them. Only the true God can sustain. Everything else crumbles.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
